segments.speaker: odysseus
segments.caption: Cyclops! It was no weak man's friends you ate in your hollow cave — your evil deeds were bound to find you out! You dared devour guests in your own house, and Zeus and the gods have paid you for it!
segments.delivery: victorious self-control collapsing into identity-driven boasting and irreversible disclosure

segments.caption: Polyphemus tears off a mountain peak and hurls it, driving a wave that nearly beaches the ship again.
segments.delivery: blind shore figure orienting by voice, hurling landscape, remembering prophecy, and praying to his father

segments.speaker: odysseus
segments.caption: Cyclops — if any mortal ever asks who put out your eye so shamefully, tell him this: it was Odysseus, sacker of cities, who blinded you — Laertes's son, whose home is in Ithaca!
segments.delivery: victorious self-control collapsing into identity-driven boasting and irreversible disclosure

segments.caption: Polyphemus
segments.delivery: blind shore figure orienting by voice, hurling landscape, remembering prophecy, and praying to his father

segments.caption: So the old prophecy comes home — Telemus foretold I would lose my sight at the hands of Odysseus, and I watched all these years for a great man, not this little worthless nothing who undid me with wine. Hear me, Poseidon, dark-haired shaker of the earth, if I am truly your son: grant that Odysseus, sacker of cities, never reach his home. Or if he must, let him come late and broken, on a stranger's ship, all his comrades lost — and find trouble waiting in his house.
segments.delivery: blind shore figure orienting by voice, hurling landscape, remembering prophecy, and praying to his father
